newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen up $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt higher than Monday's tops, lifted by strengthening pork prices and light marketings, livestock dealers said.

Expected gains also were attributed to strong demand from packers building pork inventories in anticipation of increased business with Japan and South Korea following Thursday's announced ban on Taiwanese pork shipments.
Top prices for interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs delivered to plants were seen ranging from $50.50 to $51.00, sources there said.
The top price there Monday was $50.00, up $2.50 since Thursday when the Taiwan news broke.

Illinois top prices for hogs at plants were seen at $51.00-$52.00, sources there said. Indiana/Ohio top prices could range from $50.00 to $51.00 for hogs delivered to the plant, dealers and packer buyers in that area said.

Marketings were seen light for another day or two as producers slow hog movement amid outlooks for higher prices, some sources said. But any hogs held back will need to be marketed by midweek before they get too heavy.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Friday totalled 98,000 head, under the 100,000-head estimate, USDA said. Monday's estimate was 100,000 head.
